olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $p$ be odd prime. The sequence $(a_n)_{n\geq 0}$ starts $0,1,\ldots,p-2$ and for $n\geq p-1$, $a_n$ is the least positive integer not forming an arithmetic progression of length $p$ with any earlier terms. Prove $a_n$ equals $n$ written in base $p-1$ and read in base $p$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1995

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A calculator with only sin, cos, tan and their inverses (initially displaying 0). Given any positive rational $q$, show pressing finitely many buttons yields $q$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1995

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Nonisosceles, nonright $\triangle ABC$ with circumcenter $O$, midpoints $A_1,B_1,C_1$ of sides. $A_2$ on ray $OA_1$ with $\triangle OAA_1\sim\triangle OA_2A$; $B_2,C_2$ defined similarly. Prove $AA_2,BB_2,CC_2$ are concurrent.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1995

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Suppose $(q_n)_{n\geq 0}$ is an integer sequence with (i) $m-n\mid q_m-q_n$ for $m>n\geq 0$, and (ii) $|q_n|<P(n)$ for some polynomial $P$. Prove there is a polynomial $Q$ with $q_n=Q(n)$ for all $n$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1995

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A society of $n$ persons and $q$ amicable pairs: for every three persons at least one pair is hostile. Prove some person's foes include $\leq q(1-4q/n^2)$ amicable pairs.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1995
